history.period: 1857 revolt; memorials established in the modern era
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. No documented Hindu temple dedicated to Veer Kunwar Singh exists in Arrah; the row almost certainly refers to his memorial statue and park at Babu Veer Kunwar Singh Ramna Maidan in Arrah - a 60-acre urban park whose coordinates (25.561667, 84.664167 per Wikipedia) match the geocoded 'Veer Kunwar Singh, Arrah' POI (25.56304, 84.66426) - plus a 21-ft bronze statue near Kaimnagar on the Ara-Patna four-lane road. Veer Kunwar Singh (1777-1858), the Ujjainiya Rajput zamindar of Jagdishpur, led Bihar's 1857 revolt at age 80, briefly liberated Arrah, won his final battle near Jagdishpur on 23 April 1858 and died three days later. He is commemorated with a commemorative stamp (1966), Veer Kunwar Singh University Arrah (1992) and the Veer Kunwar Singh Setu. Retained here as a memorial record pending the keep-or-drop decision.

name: Veer Kunwar Singh Memorial (not a temple)
town_description: Arrah (Ara) is the headquarters of Bhojpur district in western Bihar, on the Son river plains; it was the centre of Kunwar Singh's 1857 revolt and hosts his university, memorial park and statue.

travel.airport: Jay Prakash Narayan International Airport, Patna (~60 km).
travel.railway: Ara Junction on the Delhi-Howrah main line, in the town.
travel.road: On NH-30/NH-84; the Ramna Maidan memorial is inside Arrah town, reached by auto/taxi.
